Smoooth vs Coolify: Infrastructure Runtimes for AI Coding Agents

Developers evaluating self-hosted infrastructure tools face two fundamentally different architectural paths: a comprehensive, human-centric web platform or a minimal, agent-native runtime. This guide provides an evidence-backed comparison between Smoooth and Coolify, examining how each system approaches Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflows, resource overhead, deployment rollbacks, and operational complexity.

Type: Architectural Evaluation · Scope: Single-Server Linux VPS & MCP · Last Updated: October 2026

Executive Summary: Choosing the Right Tool

Both Smoooth and Coolify enable developers to run applications on self-hosted servers without proprietary cloud PaaS vendor lock-in. However, their core designs serve different workflows:

Consider Smoooth if:

  • You use AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) as your primary deployment and DevOps operator.
  • You want an agent-native runtime with a 2-phase transactional DAG that automatically rolls back failed deployments.
  • You run workloads on budget or low-overhead VPS instances (1 vCPU, 1–2 GB RAM) where minimal host control plane overhead is required.
  • You prefer zero-open-port loopback bindings (127.0.0.1:4040) and 256-bit scoped bearer tokens over a public web UI.

Consider Coolify if:

  • You want a rich web UI dashboard for manual point-and-click configuration, monitoring, and team member management.
  • You need a catalog of 300+ one-click open-source templates (e.g. WordPress, Plausible, Ghost, Mastodon).
  • You manage multi-server clusters or remote Docker instances from a single central control plane.
  • You prefer integrated Git push-to-deploy webhooks without requiring an active AI coding agent or CI CLI pipeline.

How Smoooth's Agent-Driven Workflow Works

In traditional PaaS architectures, deploying an application requires an engineer to open a browser, click through dashboard dialogs, paste environment variables, and monitor build logs. When teams introduce AI coding agents like Claude Code or Cursor into this setup, the agent is often forced to either interact with complex REST APIs or simulate human actions.

Smoooth takes a fundamentally different approach by making the AI coding agent the first-class deployment driver via the Model Context Protocol (MCP):

  1. Structured Planning: Instead of executing unstructured bash commands or guessing API calls, the agent invokes create_plan. Smoooth compiles a validated directed acyclic graph (DAG) specifying container lifecycle events, persistent volume allocations, and ingress mappings.
  2. Cryptographic Governance: The plan generates an immutable SHA-256 canonical plan hash. In high-governance environments, autonomous execution can be fenced until an administrator explicitly signs off on that exact hash.
  3. Guaranteed Rollback: When the agent calls execute_plan, Smoooth executes actions transactionally. If the newly booted container fails its HTTP or TCP health check, Smoooth automatically halts execution, reverts proxy configurations, and preserves existing database states.

When Coolify is the Better Choice

Coolify is one of the most popular and mature open-source self-hosted PaaS projects available today, and for many teams, it is the superior choice over Smoooth. You should pick Coolify if your workflow benefits from:

  • A Graphic Management Interface: If non-technical teammates, product managers, or developers who prefer visual dashboards need to inspect server health, restart crashed containers, or update environment variables without using a terminal or AI CLI.
  • One-Click App Catalog: Coolify provides over 300 pre-configured application templates—ranging from analytics engines (Plausible, Umami) to CMS platforms (Ghost, WordPress) and message queues. Smoooth focuses strictly on deploying custom application code and core databases.
  • Multi-Server Control Plane: Coolify allows a single central instance to connect over SSH to multiple remote servers, deploying workloads across separate machines. Smoooth v0.1.0 is engineered as a host-local runtime daemon dedicated to the server on which it runs.
  • Built-In S3 Database Backups: Coolify includes a native automated backup scheduler that executes database dumps and uploads them directly to Amazon S3 or compatible object storage on a cron schedule.

Migration Between Platforms

Because both platforms rely on standard Docker containers and host volume mounts rather than proprietary runtime abstractions, migrating between them does not lock your data into a proprietary format.

Smoooth includes a native migration scanner (smoooth migrate scan-host) designed to inspect running containers on an existing host, detect Docker Compose labels, identify volume storage paths, and translate Traefik ingress rules into Caddy configurations without dropping active network connections.
